headline: A Chinese memory-chip maker, YMTC, is reported to expect memory shortages to run for three more years and has begun raising its own prices.
score_reason: Kept at the pool level: a widely repeated forecast from a large NAND maker, but second-hand and with unclear attribution.
importance_line: Buyers of phones, computers and storage drives may keep paying more for memory if the shortage lasts that long, but the forecast is second-hand and one outlet attributes it to a single employee.
source: The Wire China, as relayed by TechPowerUp and eTeknix
summary: The Wire China reports, as relayed by TechPowerUp and eTeknix, that YMTC, a Chinese maker of NAND flash memory, the type used in phones and storage drives, expects the global memory shortage to last another three years. eTeknix adds that YMTC, the world's fourth-largest NAND maker with about 14% of the market, has already begun raising prices and is moving toward the more profitable data-centre market; one other outlet's headline attributes the view to a YMTC employee.
notes: Credit chain: The Wire China (original, not opened) to TechPowerUp (pool item, HTTP 403) to eTeknix (page read, so the url is eTeknix). The specific Wire China article link was not found. XenoSpectrum's headline says 'YMTC employee'; eTeknix says the company. Single original source.
